subject: Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples?

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples?
parts:
Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples? I'm using rtsan and I noticed that if I increase the amount of test data for which I compute log_lik in generated quantities block the computation time, the computation time increases same amount for Warm-up and Sampling (as reported by rstan). But if warm-up samples are not stored it seems that there is no sense in computing generated quantities for the.

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples?
parts:
Already an issue for this in stan-dev/stan. It can be
controlled from the interface level because there's
a flag in the write_array function that's generated that
explicitly controls whether to generate the generated
quantities or not. The reason it's there is that you
don't need them for the intermediate leapfrog steps,
but we could use it for this, too.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples?
parts:
It’s not accessible by users, but the designers of the interfaces.
For example, in CmdStan generated quantities are not computed
during warmup unless save_warmup is set to 1.

On Nov 27, 2016, at 5:38 AM, Aki Vehtari <aki.v...@aalto.fi> wrote:

I didn't understand this. "It can be controlled from the interface level", but it seems it's not possible for users?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Is generated quantities computed for warm-up samples?
parts:
On Sunday, November 27, 2016 at 4:59:19 PM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
It’s not accessible by users, but the designers of the interfaces.
For example, in CmdStan generated quantities are not computed
during warmup unless save_warmup is set to 1.

It turns out that generate_transitions() is being called the same way in rstan, so you just need to call it with save_warmup = FALSE (which is the default in CmdStan but not in RStan). But we need to add a similar mechanism in Stan for optimizing and VB.

Ben

On Friday, December 2, 2016 at 2:29:45 PM UTC-5, Aki Vehtari wrote:
I'm confused. I have rstan in two different computers and both have the same version

> packageVersion("rstan")
[1] ‘2.12.1’

> packageVersion("rstan")
[1] ‘2.12.1’

In one computer save_warmup = FALSE works and in the another  computer I get an error
Error: passing unknown arguments: save_warmup.          

Any hints how to diagnose where the problem is?

I think the one that throws an error has an incomplete uninstallation / installation of rstan 2.12.1. So, I would do

remove.packages("rstan")
system.file("libs", package = "rstan")
# make sure this is ""; otherwise remove the whole rstan directory manually
Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = "-j8") # or whatever number of cores you have
install.packages("rstan")

Ben
